$schema_note: Eval-case definitions for gnd-model-from-text. Claude reads this in-session, runs each case, and compares against expected. Adapted from the source skill's eval convention; outputs are the GND pair (model.orm.yaml + model.verbalization.txt) and every emitted model must validate via gnd.
pass_bar: T-E1 must pass on the synthetic_good_user dialogue; T-E2 coverage targets met per exercise; T-E3 and T-E4 pass on manual review; T-E5 pass with at least one stakeholder. Every emitted model.orm.yaml must exit 0 through `gnd validate` (two-layer); where gnd is not installed, the skill-bundled fallback `uv run <skill-dir>/scripts/validate_model.py` covers layer-1 structural validation only (resolve <skill-dir> to this skill's own directory).
future_work: Additional dialogue fixtures (paraphrased Halpin Workbook exercises; sparse-user and novice-user degradation fixtures) are planned but not yet authored — add them under fixtures/ with a README each and register them here when they exist.

cases.description: Synthetic dialogue with a well-engaged user (provides examples, answers clarifying questions, distinguishes alethic from deontic).
cases.equivalence: Structural match: same object_type ids (modulo naming), same fact_type shapes, same constraint types per fact type, same modality assignments. Exact provenance wording may differ.

cases.description: Count constraints by source category per exercise; verify each category meets its target.

targets.explicit: >= 60% of total constraints (CSDP is dialogue-driven; explicit constraints from user statements dominate)
targets.sample: >= 1 constraint per exercise when the fixture leaves a sample-only pattern unconfirmed (small Halpin populations should yield at least one; a fully-engaged user may confirm them all into explicit)
targets.common-sense: >= 40% of expected count (library hits on common object-type names)
targets.llm-inferred: >= 1 proposal per exercise with rationale_world_fact populated; >= 50% rejected at 6d/7b (LLM is highest-hallucination-risk source)
targets.user-supplied: >= 1 per exercise (CSDP Step 7d should typically surface at least one missed rule)

modality_targets.every_constraint_has_modality: 100% — the meta-schema requires it; validation exit 0 is the mechanical proof
modality_targets.unconfirmed_inferred_alethic: 0 — no proposed llm-inferred/common-sense constraint may carry alethic (semantic:modality-policy warning must not fire)

cases.description: Manual review of Claude's question-asking quality at ambiguous CSDP steps.
review_criteria: Did Claude elicit reference schemes explicitly (vs assuming attribute thinking)? Especially: was each new entity type's reference mode chosen by an explicit user decision?
Did Claude verbalize each fact as a question, never as an assertion?
Did Claude push back on premature subtyping using the Halpin role-based criterion?
Did Claude decompose compound predicates into elementary facts?
Did Claude redirect ER vocabulary (table/column/attribute) to Halpin terms (fact type/role/object type)?
cases.pass: All five criteria pass on manual review across all T-E1 cases.

cases.description: Manual review of Halpin-posture adherence — terminology, atomic decomposition, fact-based thinking.
review_criteria: All emitted YAML uses Halpin vocabulary (fact_type, object_type, reference mode, role, etc.) — never ER vocabulary (table, column, attribute, relationship type, junction)
All fact types are atomic (no compound predicates)
No subtypes are emitted whose justification is attribute-based rather than role-based
Sample populations rendered in the verbalization (when present in YAML)
User quotes cited in provenance for source=explicit and source=user-supplied constraints

cases.description: Hand the verbalization to a stakeholder with no ORM background; can they validate the model by reading verbalizations?
cases.method: Run CSDP on one of the T-E1 fixtures. Hand the resulting model.verbalization.txt to a domain expert who is NOT familiar with ORM 2 notation, Halpin's textbook, or the GND tooling. Have them fill in evals/reviewability_checklist.md.
cases.pass: At least one stakeholder confirms they can validate the model without help (no need to see the YAML or original dialogue).

running_evals.manual_methodology: Claude runs CSDP on each fixture in-session, writes outputs to evals/results/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<exercise>/{output.orm.yaml, output.verbalization.txt, diff.md}, validates output.orm.yaml with both validators, then produces a per-case verdict comparing against the expected reference and the pass criteria.
running_evals.diff_format: diff.md per run: (1) T-E1 structural diff, (2) T-E2 source-category counts vs targets (incl. modality targets), (3) T-E3 question-asking review with concrete examples, (4) T-E4 posture-adherence review, (5) overall pass/fail.
running_evals.automation_status: manual for now. Stretch goal — eval runner if the fixture count grows.
